title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The cote is the 1976 IHÉS talk on the divided-power de Rham complex. The manuscript is written on the backs of typed SGA 7 IX pages (Néron models and the monodromy pairing; Lie algebra and exponential), so the neighbouring 'pages' are unrelated typescript.

What this page proves. It is a 'canonicity' or 'independence of choices' argument. For a sheaf of rings or modules h on a site or space X, Grothendieck considers a category DR_gr(X,h)_0 of auxiliary data used to build a graded divided-power de Rham complex DR(L,T). The data are presentations
  0 -> h -> L -> Ψ -> 0,
with L flat and Ψ h-flat. From such a presentation one forms DR(L,T), a Koszul-type complex built from the divided powers Γ^k L (and exterior or symmetric powers of the other term). This is the familiar divided-power Koszul complex Γ^{n-i}(·) ⊗ Λ^i(·) attached to a linear map.

The argument has three steps.
1. A category of such data, localised or 'derived' with respect to the relevant weak equivalences, is already known to be equivalent to the punctual category (a point). So DR_gr(X,h)_0 is contractible: the construction is independent of choices up to unique isomorphism.
2. He then restricts to the subcategory 'DR gr plat' in which the L are flasque, with the Γ^i L flasque for i>0 (the crossed-out parenthetical). He makes an explicit hypothesis: if L is flat and 'universally flasque', then the Γ^k L (k>0) are universally flasque. Under it, DR(L,T) is again (universally) flasque. As before, the derived category in question is equivalent to the one built from universally flasque L with L/hT flat (the exact sequences above, with L universally flasque and Ψ h-flat), and that category is again punctual.
3. Proposition. DR_gr(X,h)_0 is equivalent to the punctual category. The same holds for DR gr plat(X,h)_0, provided that for every flat, universally flasque h-module L the Γ^i L (i>0) are universally flasque.

What it serves. Its role is to show that the flasque, hence cohomologically computable, model of the divided-power de Rham complex is canonical in the derived category. Hypercohomology can then be computed with flasque objects without the result depending on choices.
errors: The key step is not proved but explicitly assumed ('Supposons que ceci implique...'): that the divided powers Γ^i of a flat, (universally) flasque module are again (universally) flasque. This is not automatic, because tensor and symmetric constructions on sheaves do not preserve flasqueness in general. The final Proposition is accordingly stated conditionally, and the gap is acknowledged rather than an error.

The notion 'universellement flasque' is not defined on the page. It presumably means flasque after any base change, or such that all relevant tensor constructions are flasque. Without the definition, the argument cannot be fully checked.
Step 1 relies on 'on sait que cette dernière est équivalente à la cat. ponctuelle' from the previous manuscript page, which is not available here.

ideas.what: Category of choices (presentations/resolutions) used to construct a complex is contractible (equivalent to the punctual category), so the construction is canonical up to unique isomorphism
ideas.modern_name: contractibility of the category/space of resolutions; homotopy-coherent independence of choices
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard technique (Illusie's Complexe cotangent, Deligne's Hodge III, later ∞-categorical formulations)
ideas.where_published: Contractibility-of-choices philosophy pervades Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs; this specific instance is unpublished

ideas.what: Divided-power (Koszul-type) de Rham complex DR(L,T) built from Γ^k L for a presentation 0->h->L->Ψ->0
ideas.modern_name: divided-power Koszul complex / derived divided powers; precursor of derived de Rham / crystalline comparisons
ideas.usually_credited_to: Illusie (Complexe cotangent et déformations, 1971-72) for Koszul complexes with Γ and Λ; Berthelot for divided-power de Rham complexes; Bhatt (2012) for derived de Rham

ideas.what: Hypothesis that divided powers of flat universally flasque modules remain universally flasque, used to get flasque models of DR
ideas.modern_name: preservation of flasque/acyclic objects under nonadditive (polynomial) functors

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether Γ^i of a flat 'universally flasque' module is universally flasque. This is needed for a flasque, choice-independent model of the divided-power de Rham complex. The Proposition is stated conditionally on it.
missed.quote: si on suppose que h-module L plat et univ. flasque, les Γ^i L (i>0) sont aussi univ. flasques.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a small technical gap about acyclic resolutions for nonadditive functors on sheaves. Today it is usually bypassed with simplicial or ∞-categorical methods (derived functors of Γ via Dold–Puppe), so it is mainly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine canonicity argument (the category of choices is contractible) with an explicitly flagged technical hypothesis. It documents the content of an unpublished 1976 lecture but contains no striking result beyond standard techniques.
transcription_corrections: 'avec des $A_n$[?] flasques' is more likely 'avec des $\mathcal{L}$ flasques'.
The struck-out parenthetical '($A^i$[?] flasque si $i<j$[?])' plausibly reads '(i.e. $\Gamma^i\mathcal{L}$ flasques si $i>0$)'.
The exact sequence is likely '$0\to h\to\mathcal{L}\to\Psi\to 0$'.
'construite avec [-les cat. des-] $\mathcal{L}$ univ. flasques de $DR(\mathcal{L},T)$' should probably read 'construite avec les $\mathcal{L}$ univ. flasques et $DR(\mathcal{L},T)$'.
'$\Gamma_k$' and '$\Gamma^i$' denote the same divided powers; the transcription mixes the two indices.
